title: Rejection and non-negativity
objective: Name the fact each branch of a transfer proof uses, and say which axioms automation adds to a proof.

choice.prompt: `grind` and `omega` each close `transfer_conserves`. Do the two proofs depend on the same axioms?

options.text: Yes: a theorem has one axiom list.
options.why: The list belongs to the proof, not to the theorem.
As recorded in {{run:RUN-lean-axioms}}.
The `omega` proof lists `propext` and `Quot.sound` {{run:RUN-lean-axioms}}.
`sorryAx` marks an unfinished proof, and neither is unfinished.

blocks.md:
A transfer proof splits in two. In the allowed branch the guard holds, the balances change, and the proof does arithmetic. In the rejected branch the guard fails and the transfer hands back the state it was given. That second branch has a fixed shape: every rejection theorem has one hypothesis, that the guard fails, and one conclusion, that nothing changed.

```lean
theorem transferPos_rejected (s : Ledger) (n : Int) (h : ¬ (0 < n ∧ n ≤ s.a)) :
    transferPos s n = s
```

`transferPos` is the transfer from earlier in this stage with a stricter guard: it also rejects a zero amount. It runs parallel to the transfer in LAB-2, so the proof below uses the moves you will need there without being a proof you will write. Read it as a manual proof, and watch which line uses which fact.

blocks.direction: Replay shows: the proof one tactic at a time with the goal after each, then the axioms the finished proof depends on. No tactic in it is automation.

code.text:
structure Ledger where
  a : Int
  b : Int
deriving Repr, DecidableEq

def transferPos (s : Ledger) (n : Int) : Ledger :=
  if 0 < n ∧ n ≤ s.a then { a := s.a - n, b := s.b + n } else s

theorem transferPos_nonneg (s : Ledger) (n : Int) (ha : 0 ≤ s.a) (hb : 0 ≤ s.b) :
    0 ≤ (transferPos s n).a ∧ 0 ≤ (transferPos s n).b := by
  unfold transferPos
  split
  · next hg => exact ⟨Int.sub_nonneg_of_le hg.2, Int.add_nonneg hb (Int.le_of_lt hg.1)⟩
  · exact ⟨ha, hb⟩

#print axioms transferPos_nonneg

tap.property: both balances are non-negative after an allowed transfer

call.prompt: In the allowed branch, which fact makes `0 ≤ s.a - n` true?

options.why: Not needed here: `n ≤ s.a` alone gives `0 ≤ s.a - n`. `ha` serves the rejected branch.
Taking away at most `s.a` leaves at least 0.
That is a fact about the recipient.
It serves the recipient's half, not the sender's.

blocks.after: Each half of the allowed branch has its own fact: `n ≤ s.a` for the sender, `hb` and `0 < n` for the recipient. The rejected branch uses no guard fact at all. The state is unchanged, so `ha` and `hb` already are the goal. That is what unchanged on rejection looks like inside a proof.

blocks.md: Automation can hide all of this. `omega` closes goals of linear integer arithmetic. `grind` is a general solver whose proofs can use more axioms than a manual proof does {{run:RUN-lean-axioms}}. `decide` evaluates a closed goal. Each can finish the step you are meant to learn, and each can change the axiom list a stamp carries. So LAB-2.3 and LAB-2.4 run in manual mode: the check wants a proof with none of them in the theorem it teaches. The rest of the course stays open.

choice.prompt: In `transferPos_nonneg`, the allowed branch must show `0 ≤ s.b + n`. Which facts does it use?

options.why: Those serve the sender's half.
`hb` alone does not rule out a negative `n`.
A non-negative balance plus a positive amount is non-negative.
It bounds the amount above and says nothing about the recipient's balance.

choice.prompt: A receipt for a `grind` proof prints `'transferPos_conserves_grind' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` {{run:RUN-lean-s2-cells}}, and the scan finds `grind`. Complete the stamp: PROVED [P] · Lean 4.35.0 kernel · axioms listed: …

options.why: The stamp lists what the receipt printed, and the flag says automation did the work.
That is the `omega` proof's list. This receipt printed three axioms.
A proof with no axioms says so, and this receipt printed three.
`sorryAx` marks an unfinished proof, and this one is finished.

choice.prompt: To prove `transferPos s n = s`, which fact turns the `if` into its `else` branch?

options.why: Nothing about the sender's balance decides the guard.

options.text: The guard itself, `0 < n ∧ n ≤ s.a`
options.why: That is the allowed branch's fact. Here the guard fails.
The recipient's balance is not part of the guard.
It rules out the allowed branch, so the `else` branch is the only one left.

choice.prompt: A receipt for the manual proof of `transferPos_nonneg` prints `'transferPos_nonneg' depends on axioms: [propext]` {{run:RUN-lean-s2-cells}}, and the scan finds no automation. Complete the qualifier.

options.why: Not every proof lists the same two. This receipt printed one.
A manual proof can still use an axiom, and this one printed `propext`.
The qualifier copies the receipt, and the scan found no automation.
The scan found no automation. Arithmetic closed by hand is not `omega`.

blocks.md: Two claim cards come out of this pair, non-negativity and unchanged on rejection. The lab stages mint them from proofs you write.
